## Introduction

The `sorter2r` package provides R wrappers for the
[SORTER2](https://github.com/KEW-SORTER/SORTER2) Python pipeline, which
assembles and phases allopolyploid sequences from target-capture
sequencing data. The pipeline runs a series of computationally intensive
steps—SPAdes assembly, read mapping, haplotype phasing—that can take
hours to complete on real datasets.

The [{targets}](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/) package is a natural
fit: it tracks the inputs and outputs of each stage and re-runs only the
stages whose inputs have changed since the last successful run, making
long pipelines both reproducible and efficient.

This vignette walks through a complete sorter2r pipeline using {targets}.

## Prerequisites

The following software must be installed before running the pipeline.

**Python tools** (install in a conda environment, typically named
`"SORTER2"`):

- [SORTER2](https://github.com/KEW-SORTER/SORTER2)
- [SPAdes](https://github.com/ablab/spades) (genome assembler)
- [bwa](https://github.com/lh3/bwa) (read mapper)
- [samtools](https://www.htslib.org/) (SAM/BAM utilities)
- [MAFFT](https://mafft.cbrc.jp/alignment/software/) (multiple
  sequence aligner)
- [vsearch](https://github.com/torognes/vsearch) or usearch
  (sequence clustering)

**R packages**:

```r
install.packages(c("targets", "tarchetypes"))
remotes::install_github("joelnitta/sorter2r")
```

**Environment variables** (optional but recommended; avoids repeating
`conda_env = "SORTER2"` in every call):

```r
Sys.setenv(SORTER2R_CONDA_ENV = "SORTER2")
```

## Input data layout

sorter2r expects paired-end FASTQ files in a single directory, with
filenames following the pattern `<sample>_R1.fastq` / `<sample>_R2.fastq`:


``` r
list.files(file.path(mini, "fastq"))
#>  [1] "Iimura12_cthysanostomum_R1.fastq" "Iimura12_cthysanostomum_R2.fastq"
#>  [3] "Iimura18_cthysanostomum_R1.fastq" "Iimura18_cthysanostomum_R2.fastq"
#>  [5] "Iimura46_cgrande_R1.fastq"        "Iimura46_cgrande_R2.fastq"       
#>  [7] "Liu18_cthysanostomum_R1.fastq"    "Liu18_cthysanostomum_R2.fastq"   
#>  [9] "Wade3565_cintermedium_R1.fastq"   "Wade3565_cintermedium_R2.fastq"
```

You also need a SORTER2 reference FASTA (a set of target loci) and,
for organellar recovery with `sorter2_haplominer()`, a haploid
organellar reference such as a complete plastome.

## Defining the pipeline

Create a `_targets.R` file in your project root. The pipeline flows
linearly: each stage reads its predecessor's output directory and writes
to its own dedicated output directory, ensuring {targets} can detect
changes reliably.


``` r
library(targets)
library(tarchetypes)
library(sorter2r)

list(
  # Input files ----
  tar_file(reads_dir, "data/fastq"),
  tar_file(ref, "data/reference/sorter2.fasta"),
  tar_file(plastome_ref, "data/reference/plastome.fasta"),

  # Stage 1A: assemble reads with SPAdes ----
  tar_file(
    stage1a,
    sorter2_stage1a(
      reads_dir  = reads_dir,
      output_dir = "results/stage1a",
      trim       = FALSE,
      spades     = TRUE,
      conda_env  = "SORTER2"
    )
  ),

  # Filter to ingroup assemblies only ----
  tar_file(
    ingroup_assemblies,
    sorter2_filter_assemblies(
      input_dir       = stage1a,
      output_dir      = "results/stage1a_ingroups",
      exclude_samples = c("outgroup_sample1")
    )
  ),

  # Stage 1B: cluster loci ----
  tar_file(
    stage1b,
    sorter2_stage1b(
      input_dir  = ingroup_assemblies,
      output_dir = "results/stage1b",
      ref        = ref,
      loci       = 479L,
      conda_env  = "SORTER2"
    )
  ),

  # Infer hybrid candidates from cluster pattern ----
  tar_target(
    hybrids,
    sorter2_infer_hybrids(stage1b)
  ),

  # Stage 2: phase orthologs ----
  tar_file(
    stage2,
    sorter2_stage2(
      input_assemblies = ingroup_assemblies,
      input_clusters   = stage1b,
      output_dir       = "results/stage2",
      reads_dir        = reads_dir,
      threads          = 6L,
      conda_env        = "SORTER2"
    )
  ),

  # Stage 3: phase hybrids ----
  tar_file(
    stage3,
    sorter2_stage3(
      input_phased     = stage2,
      input_assemblies = ingroup_assemblies,
      output_dir       = "results/stage3",
      phaseset_dir     = ingroup_assemblies,
      hybrid_samples   = hybrids$sample[hybrids$candidate],
      reads_dir        = reads_dir,
      ref              = ref,
      loci             = 479L,
      conda_env        = "SORTER2"
    )
  ),

  # Summarize progenitor sequences ----
  tar_file(
    progenitor_res,
    sorter2_progenitor_processor(
      input_dir  = file.path(
        stage3, "phaseset", "diploidclusters_phased"
      ),
      output_dir = "results/progenitor",
      mapfile    = "data/reference/progenitor_map.csv",
      outgroups  = "data/reference/outgroups.txt",
      conda_env  = "SORTER2"
    )
  ),

  # Processor: filter and summarize final alignments ----
  tar_file(
    processor_res,
    sorter2_processor(
      input_dir  = stage1b,
      output_dir = "results/processor",
      conda_env  = "SORTER2"
    )
  ),

  # Hapl-O-Miner: recover organellar sequences ----
  tar_file(
    haplominer_res,
    sorter2_haplominer(
      input_dir       = stage1a,
      output_dir      = "results/haplominer",
      organellar_ref  = plastome_ref,
      reads_dir       = reads_dir,
      threads         = 6L,
      clean_workfiles = TRUE,
      conda_env       = "SORTER2"
    )
  )
)
```

`tar_file()` (from {tarchetypes}) is shorthand for
`tar_target(..., format = "file")`. It tells {targets} to track an
output directory by hashing its contents; any change to the directory
invalidates the target and triggers a re-run downstream.

## Running the pipeline

Call `tar_make()` to execute all targets in dependency order:


``` r
targets::tar_make(script = script, store = store)
#> + processor_res dispatched
#> ✖ processor_res errored
#> ✖ errored pipeline [385ms, 0 completed, 9 skipped]
#> Error:
#> ! Error in tar_make():
#>   Output already exists: /home/jnitta/sorter2r/inst/dev-data-mini/processor
#> Set overwrite = TRUE to remove it and re-run.
#>   See https://books.ropensci.org/targets/debugging.html
```

## Caching: subsequent runs

On a second `tar_make()` call, {targets} checks every target's inputs.
Because nothing has changed, every target is skipped:


``` r
targets::tar_make(script = script, store = store)
#> + processor_res dispatched
#> ✖ processor_res errored
#> ✖ errored pipeline [290ms, 0 completed, 9 skipped]
#> Error:
#> ! Error in tar_make():
#>   Output already exists: /home/jnitta/sorter2r/inst/dev-data-mini/processor
#> Set overwrite = TRUE to remove it and re-run.
#>   See https://books.ropensci.org/targets/debugging.html
```

This caching is especially valuable for long-running pipelines: if a
stage fails partway through, only that stage (and its dependents)
re-runs on the next `tar_make()`.

## Inspecting the pipeline

`tar_manifest()` lists all targets and their dependencies without
running anything—useful for checking the pipeline structure before a
long run or after modifying `_targets.R`:


``` r
targets::tar_manifest(
  script         = script,
  callr_function = NULL
)
#> # A tibble: 12 × 2
#>    name               command                                                   
#>    <chr>              <chr>                                                     
#>  1 reads              "file.path(mini, \"fastq\")"                              
#>  2 plastome_ref       "file.path(mini, \"reference\", \"Crepidomanes_minutum_NC…
#>  3 ref                "file.path(mini, \"reference\", \"fermaily_perfamily2hybp…
#>  4 stage1a            "sorter2_stage1a(reads_dir = reads, output_dir = file.pat…
#>  5 ingroup_assemblies "sorter2_filter_assemblies(input_dir = stage1a, output_di…
#>  6 haplominer_res     "sorter2_haplominer(input_dir = stage1a, output_dir = fil…
#>  7 stage1b            "sorter2_stage1b(input_dir = ingroup_assemblies, output_d…
#>  8 stage2             "sorter2_stage2(input_assemblies = ingroup_assemblies, \n…
#>  9 hybrids            "sorter2_infer_hybrids(stage1b)"                          
#> 10 processor_res      "sorter2_processor(input_dir = stage1b, output_dir = file…
#> 11 stage3             "sorter2_stage3(input_phased = stage2, input_assemblies =…
#> 12 progenitor_res     "sorter2_progenitor_processor(input_dir = file.path(stage…
```

## Examining results

### Stage 2: read-mapping statistics

Stage 2 writes a `readstats_fin.csv` with per-sample read-mapping
metrics. The `readdepth` and `coverage` columns show mean read depth
and the percentage of the reference covered, respectively:


``` r
readstats <- read.csv(
  file.path(mini, "stage2", "readstats_fin.csv")
)
readstats[, c("Individual", "mapped", "coverage")]
#>                Individual mapped coverage
#> 1 Iimura18_cthysanostomum   1662       12
#> 2    Liu18_cthysanostomum   1662       12
#> 3        Iimura46_cgrande   4237       19
#> 4 Iimura12_cthysanostomum   1067       11
```

### Hybrid candidate inference

`sorter2_infer_hybrids()` inspects the Stage 1B clustering pattern and
returns a data frame flagging samples whose pattern is consistent with
allopolyploidy:


``` r
targets::tar_read(hybrids, store = store)
#>                    sample total_alleles n_loci mean_per_locus candidate
#> 3        Iimura46_cgrande            41      7           5.86      TRUE
#> 2 Iimura18_cthysanostomum            27      9           3.00      TRUE
#> 4    Liu18_cthysanostomum            27      9           3.00      TRUE
#> 1 Iimura12_cthysanostomum            16      9           1.78     FALSE
```

### Hapl-O-Miner: organellar sequence recovery

`sorter2_haplominer()` maps reads to a haploid organellar reference and
assembles per-sample consensus sequences. With `clean_workfiles = TRUE`,
intermediate BAM files are removed after the run to save disk space.

Consensus sequences that pass the coverage and depth thresholds:


``` r
list.files(file.path(mini, "haplominer", "all_chloroplasts"))
#> [1] "Iimura18_cthysanostomum_chloroplast.fasta"
#> [2] "Liu18_cthysanostomum_chloroplast.fasta"
```

Coverage and mean read-depth statistics for all samples:


``` r
hm_stats <- read.csv(
  file.path(mini, "haplominer", "readstats_cp.csv")
)
hm_stats[, c("Individual", "readdepth", "coverage")]
#>                Individual readdepth coverage
#> 1 Iimura18_cthysanostomum         0        0
#> 2    Liu18_cthysanostomum         0        0
#> 3        Iimura46_cgrande         0        0
#> 4 Iimura12_cthysanostomum         0        0
#> 5   Wade3565_cintermedium         0        0
```
